answer: Make every identity a vertex in a public trust graph whose edges are earned only by completed, verified work, and stamp each new vertex with an umber flag until it clears its first audited job. A newcomer starts at the tide line with zero inbound trust and must win endorsements from established vertices, each backed by a small slashable bond from the sponsor. A sybil farmer spinning up a thousand clones gets a thousand flagged, isolated vertices that send no trust signal at all, while each clone still costs its bond plus the wait for an audit. Cloning scales cost linearly; trust stays scarce.
